primary_diagnosis_treated: End-Stage Renal Disease secondary to diabetic and hypertensive nephropathy
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) & NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control and reduction of proteinuria (renoprotective)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: ACE inhibitor recommended for CKD with hypertension or proteinuria; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive and volume management in resistant hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Thiazide diuretic as part of three‑drug regimen for resistant hypertension
NG203: CCB recommended as third agent when ACE‑I and thiazide are insufficient

medications.duration: Until ferritin >200 µg/L and TSAT >20% (approximately 3 months) then review
medications.nice_justification: NG107: Iron supplementation indicated when ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20%

medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 100‑120 g/L, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG107: ESA indicated for CKD anemia with Hb <100 g/L and symptoms

medications.duration: Ongoing — adjust per HbA1c and glucose logs
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for diabetes/prediabetes with renal complications
medications.nice_justification: CKD guideline: insulin is safe in eGFR <30; oral hypoglycemics (e.g., metformin) contraindicated

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Statin recommended for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2 weeks to max 10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review BP and heart rate after each titration, then annually
medications.purpose: Add third antihypertensive agent for resistant hypertension (if BP >140/90 mmHg)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Beta‑blocker can be used as fourth‑line agent when BP remains uncontrolled on ACE‑I, thiazide and CCB

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive hypotensive effect; risk of symptomatic hypotension and bradycardia
interactions_checked.action: Start bisoprolol at low dose, monitor BP and heart rate after each titration; advise patient to rise slowly

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for enhanced blood pressure lowering and electrolyte shifts
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure and serum electrolytes after dose changes

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined antihypertensive effect may cause excessive BP drop
interactions_checked.action: Check for dizziness or orthostatic symptoms; adjust doses if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant interaction with current regimen
interactions_checked.action: Baseline CK and LFTs; monitor for myopathy

contraindications.reason: eGFR 11.5 mL/min (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
CKD stage 4 – accelerates renal decline and causes fluid retention
Guideline contraindication due to increased hyperkalaemia and AKI risk; patient only on ACE‑I
eGFR 11.5 mL/min (<20) – contraindicated for renal indication
Risk of hyperkalaemia in advanced CKD

treatment_summary: The plan continues renoprotective ACE‑I, thiazide, and CCB therapy, adds a statin (atorvastatin 20 mg) for cardiovascular risk reduction, and conditionally introduces a beta‑blocker (bisoprolol) if resistant hypertension persists. Existing anemia management with iron, epoetin alfa, and insulin is maintained. Contraindicated agents (metformin, NSAIDs, SGLT2 inhibitors) are avoided. Monitoring includes BP, heart rate, lipid profile, LFTs, CK, electrolytes, and renal function per NICE NG203/NG107.
